dervis-irab:1-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سُباتاً) Rest for your bodies. In al-Mukhtār: «al-subāt is sleep, and its origin is rest; from it is His saying, the Exalted: وجعلنا نومكم سباتا; and its pattern is naṣara.» In al-Miṣbāḥ:
«al-subāt, with ḍamma, like ghurāb: heavy sleep, and its origin is rest. From it one says sabata, yasbutu, of the pattern of qatala; and subita, in the passive: he fainted, and also: he died.» Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «سباتا: death; and al-masbūt is the dead, from al-sabt, which is cutting, because he is cut off from movement; and sleep is one of the two takings of the soul (al-tawaffiyayn); and it is on the pattern of the names of diseases.» As for Abū Ḥayyān, he said: «al-subāt is a known illness in which silence overcomes a person excessively until it becomes fatal.»
(الْمُعْصِراتِ) al-muʿṣir: al-Farrāʾ said: the clouds that bring rain but have not yet gathered, like the girl who is muʿṣir, who is about to menstruate but has not yet menstruated. Ibn Qutayba said something similar. And Abū al-Najm al-ʿIjlī said:
تمشي الهوينى مائلا خمارها ... قد أعصرت أو قد دنا إعصارها
(She walks gently, her veil leaning; she has come of age, or her coming of age has drawn near.)
And ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
فكان مجني دون من كنت أتقي ... ثلاث شخوص كاعبان ومعصر
(My shield against those I feared was three figures: two full-breasted maidens and a girl come of age.)
(ثَجَّاجاً) al-thajj: pouring down with abundance and force. In the ḥadīth: «The deed most beloved to Allah is al-ʿajj and al-thajj»; al-ʿajj is raising the voice in the talbiya and al-thajj is shedding the blood of the sacrificial animals. One says: the water thajja by itself, i.e. it poured down; and I thajajtuhu, i.e. I poured it, thajjan and thujūjan; so it is intransitive and transitive. [Translator's note: the opening quotation mark before «أحب العمل» is not closed in the source.] In al-Mukhtār: «The water and the blood thajja: flowed, and its pattern is radda; and a thajjāj rain, i.e. pouring down greatly. And al-thajj is also the flowing of the blood of sacrificial animals, and it is intransitive; you say from it: the blood thajja, yathijju (with kasra), thajjan (with fatḥa). I say: al-Azharī transmitted the like of this from Abū ʿUbayda.»
(أَلْفافاً) Intertwined. In al-Asās: «He wrapped (laffa) the garment and other things, and wrapped the thing in his garment, and laffafahu; and he wrapped his head in his clothes, and iltaffa in his clothes, and talaffafa; and the plants became intertwined (iltaffa), and in the land there are talāfīf of herbage; and جنات ألفافا: intertwined; and in it there is a thicket (lafaf) of trees. Al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:
ولقد عرتني منك جدوى أنبتت ... خضرا إلى لفف من الأشجار
(A gift from you came to me that made green things grow, up to a thicket of trees.)
And a man is alaff and a woman laffāʾ; she laffat, talaffu, lafafan, which is the closeness of the thighs from fatness; it is a defect in a man and a praise in a woman. Naṣr ibn Sayyār, ruler of Khurāsān, said:
ولو كنت القتيل وكان حيّا ... تشمّر لا ألفّ ولا سؤوم
(Had I been the slain and he alive, he would have girded himself, neither heavy-thighed nor weary.)
And he said, describing women:
عراض القطا ملتفة ربلاتها ... وما اللفّ أفخاذا بتاركة عقلا»
(Broad of rump, their inner thighs fleshy; and the full-thighed ones do not leave a mind (intact).)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «ألفافا: intertwined; it has no singular, and it is said the singular is liff, with kasra on the lām», so it would be like sirr and asrār. And it is said it is the plural of lafīf — al-Kisāʾī said that — and similar are sharīf and ashrāf, shahīd and ashhād.

* I'rab:
(عَمَّ يَتَساءَلُونَ، عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ، الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ) عن is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun, genitive (majrūr) by عن. It has preceded that the alif of interrogative ما is mostly omitted when a preposition enters upon it. And عمّا was read with the alif retained, and it has preceded that this is permissible by poetic necessity or in a small portion of speech; on this is the saying of Ḥassān ibn Thābit:
على ما قام يشتمني لئيم ... كخنزير تمرغ في رماد
(For what reason did a base man rise to revile me, like a swine rolling in ashes?)
What appears is that عمّ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يتساءلون, and the interrogative is for magnifying the matter, as if He said: about what thing are they asking one another? Similar is the like of the saying «Zayd — what is Zayd!»: you have made him, because he has no peer, as though he were something hidden from you, so you ask about his kind and examine his essence and substance; you say: what is the ghoul, and what is the ʿanqāʾ? meaning: what thing among things is this? Then it was stripped down to express magnification, until it occurred in the speech of Allah the Exalted, from whom nothing hidden is hidden. وعن النبإ العظيم is a resumed statement presented to clarify that thing, so it is attached to an omitted verb indicated by يتساءلون; it is not a complement of يتساءلون because عمّ is its complement; i.e. they are asking one another about the great news; so it is a grammatical ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). الذي is a second naʿt (adjective) of النبإ; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); فيه is attached to مختلفون, and مختلفون is the khabar (predicate) of هم, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي. (كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ) A deterrent and threat to those asking in mockery; it contains the sense of threat and menace: the deterrence with the word كلا and the threat with the word سيعلمون. The object of سيعلمون is omitted, its implied form being «what will befall them». ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay, and كلا سيعلمون is a verbal tawkīd (emphasis) of the preceding clause, and the intervention of the conjunction does no harm. The grammarians insist that it can only be a conjunction, even if it conveys emphasis; and it can be answered that there is a noticeable difference, namely that the second threat is more severe than the first; by this consideration it became different from what precedes it, and therefore it was conjoined with ثم. (أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهاداً وَالْجِبالَ أَوْتاداً) A resumed statement presented to set out His power, Glorified is He, to resurrect and to bring proofs of it; He mentioned nine of them. The point in them is that if He is able to do these things, then by plain intuition He is able to resurrect. The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), i.e. «We made the earth a resting place». لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past) and jussive; نجعل is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as «We»; الأرض is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and مهادا the second direct object, because جعل means transformation (taṣyīr). It may also mean creation, so that مهادا is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). والجبال أوتادا is conjoined to الأرض مهادا. (وَخَلَقْناكُمْ أَزْواجاً) Conjoined to what preceded. خلقناكم is a verb, its agent and its direct object; أزواجا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. of the same kind and resembling one another, males and females. (وَجَعَلْنا نَوْمَكُمْ سُباتاً) Also conjoined. جعلنا is a past verb and its agent; نومكم is the first object of جعلنا and سباتا the second object of جعلنا. (وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِباساً) Also conjoined, and the clause is like the one before it in parsing. (وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهارَ مَعاشاً) Also conjoined, and it too is like the one before it. معاشا is a mīm-maṣdar meaning livelihood, and here it has occurred as an adverb of time, i.e. a time of livelihood. (وَبَنَيْنا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعاً شِداداً)
Also conjoined. بنينا is a past verb and its agent; فوقكم is an adverb attached to بنينا; سبعا is the direct object, i.e. seven heavens; and شدادا is an adjective. (وَجَعَلْنا سِراجاً وَهَّاجاً) Also conjoined. سراجا is the object of جعلنا and وهاجا an adjective; جعل here means creation. (وَأَنْزَلْنا مِنَ الْمُعْصِراتِ ماءً ثَجَّاجاً) Also conjoined. أنزلنا is a verb and its agent; من المعصرات is attached to أنزلنا; ماء is the direct object and ثجاجا an adjective. (لِنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَباتاً) The lām is the lām of causation; نخرج is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and it is also attached to أنزلنا. به is attached to نخرج; حبا is the object of نخرج, and نباتا is conjoined to حبا. (وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفافاً) Conjoined to حبا, and the sign of its accusative is the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; ألفافا is an adjective of جنان [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has جنات], i.e. intertwined orchards.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «وجعلنا الليل لباسا» there is an eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh). The point of resemblance is covering, because each of the garment and the night covers the one who wears it; i.e. it conceals you from eyes when you want to save yourselves from an enemy pursuing you, or as a night raid on him when you want to inflict a blow on him far from eyes, or it helps you hide what you do not wish anyone to see. Abū al-Ṭayyib (al-Mutanabbī) glanced at this lofty heaven, as is his custom, and said:
وكم لظلام الليل عندك من يد ... تخبر أن المانوية تكذب
(How many a favour has the darkness of night done for you, showing that the Manichaeans lie!)
وقال رد الأعداء تسري إليهم ... وزارك فيه ذو الدلال المحجب
(It guarded you against the enemies' ruin as you marched by night to them, and in it the coy, veiled beloved visited you.) [Translator's note: the first hemistich is printed garbled in the source; the gloss follows its evident sense.]
The Manichaeans (al-Mānawiyya) are named after Mani, founder of the Manichaean doctrine of two principles in existence, a principle of good and a principle of evil: light and darkness. Mani entered into Persian painting, arranged Chinese painting and drew angels and devils, and he died in 276 CE. The explanation of the Manichaean question is that they said: you find in the world much good and much evil, and one being cannot be both good and evil; so each of good and evil has an independent agent. They said the agent of good is light and the agent of evil is darkness, and they believed that the two are eternal bodies, sentient, hearing and seeing — and all of that is manifestly false.
Abū al-Ṭayyib also said, clinging to the fringes of this lofty eloquence:
أزورهم وسواد الليل يشفع لي ... وأنثني وبياض الصبح يغري
(I visit them while the blackness of night intercedes for me, and I turn back while the whiteness of dawn incites against me.)
And Ibn Zaydūn said:
سرّان في خاطر الظلماء يكتمان ... حتى يكاد لسان الصبح يغشينا
(Two secrets kept hidden in the mind of the darkness, until the tongue of dawn almost reveals us.)

dervis-irab:17-40.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سَراباً) al-sarāb (mirage): what is seen at midday from the intensity of the heat, as though it were water in which houses, trees and other things are reflected. It is proverbial for falsehood and deception; one says «he is more deceptive than a mirage». It means that they (the mountains) become a thing like nothing, because of the dispersal of their parts and the scattering of their substances, as in His saying, the Exalted: «فانت هباء منبثا» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads فكانت هباء منبثا]. More of its meaning will come in the section on rhetoric.
(أَحْقاباً) The plural of ḥuqb (with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ), and it is also pluralized as aḥqub:
eighty years or more; and an age; and a year or years. More on what is meant by it will come in the section on i'rab.
(بَرْداً) al-bard is the touch of cold air, i.e. nothing of it touches them that they would find pleasant or that would relieve them of the day's heat. Abū ʿUbayda, al-Kisāʾī, al-Faḍl ibn Khālid and Muʿādh the grammarian said that al-bard here is sleep, and the Arabs call it so because it cools the violence of thirst; among their sayings is «the cold prevented sleep (manaʿa al-bardu al-barda)». The poet said:
فلو شئت حرّمت النساء سواكم ... وإن شئت لم أطعم نقّاخا ولا بردا
(If I wished, I would forbid myself women other than you; and if I wished, I would taste neither cool water nor sleep.)
al-nuqākh is cold water and al-bard is sleep. In the book al-Lughāt fī al-Qurʾān, al-bard is sleep in the dialect of Hudhayl. The lexicons have cited al-bard in the sense of sleep, but its occurrence with this meaning in the verse is strained. What is correct is what the majority said: that al-bard is cold drink, and it suits the word «tasting». From it is the saying:
أماني من سعدى حسان كأنما ... سقتك بها سعدى على ظمأ بردا
منى إن تكن حقا تكن أحسن المنى ... وإلّا فقد عشنا بها زمنا رغدا
(Fair hopes from Suʿdā, as though Suʿdā had given you with them a cool drink upon thirst; hopes which, if true, are the finest of hopes, and if not, we have lived by them a pleasant time.)
On this view the tasting is literal, not figurative.
(غَسَّاقاً) It was read light and with doubling. Its mention has preceded, and that it is the pus that flows from the people of the Fire.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ كانَ مِيقاتاً) A resumed statement presented to answer a question that might arise after Allah established the resurrection with the preceding proofs, namely: what is the time of the resurrection? So He said: إن يوم etc. إنّ and its noun; the clause كان is its khabar (predicate); the noun of كان is latent (mustatir), implied as «it», and ميقاتا is its predicate. (يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْواجاً) يوم is a badal (substitute) of يوم الفصل. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a substitute of ميقاتا, or accusative by an omitted verb, implied as «I mean». The clause ينفخ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. ينفخ [Translator's note: the source prints «نفخ»] is an imperfect verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, implied as «he», referring to Isrāfīl, who blows into the Trumpet. فتأتون is conjoined to ينفخ, and أفواجا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw. (وَفُتِحَتِ السَّماءُ فَكانَتْ أَبْواباً) Conjoined to فتأتون. He turned from the imperfect to the past only because of the certainty of its occurrence [Translator's note: the source says «from the past to the imperfect», evidently reversed]. It is said the wāw is circumstantial and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. you come, the state being that the sky has been opened. السماء is the deputy agent; فكانت is conjoined to فتحت; the noun of كان is latent, implied as «it», and أبوابا is its predicate. فتّحت was also read with doubling. (وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبالُ فَكانَتْ سَراباً) Also conjoined. سيّرت is a past verb, passive, and الجبال is the deputy agent; فكانت is conjoined to سيّرت, and سرابا is the predicate of كانت. (إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كانَتْ مِرْصاداً) A resumed statement presented to begin describing the terrors of Jahannam, after He finished describing the general conditions of the Day of Resurrection. إنّ and its noun; the clause كانت is its predicate; the noun of كانت is latent, implied as «it», i.e. Jahannam; and مرصادا is the predicate of كانت, i.e. lying in wait for those punished in it, watching for them; or prepared, in the sense of made ready for them. So it is either from the three-letter raṣada, meaning to watch for, or from the four-letter arṣada, i.e. to prepare. al-mirṣād in the lexicons is the road and the passage. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: al-mirṣād is the boundary at which the watching takes place. (لِلطَّاغِينَ مَآباً) للطاغين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) مرصادا [Translator's note: so in the source; given the closing sentence, «attached to مآبا» was probably meant here], and مآبا is a second predicate of كانت, i.e. a place of return for them and a destination to which they return and go back. And it is permissible to attach للطاغين to مرصاد. (لابِثِينَ فِيها أَحْقاباً) لابثين is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) of the pronoun concealed in للطاغين, and أحقابا is an adverb attached to لابثين. If it is said: the aḥqāb, however long they extend and however much time is prolonged with them, are finite in any case, whereas the punishment of the disbelievers is not finite [Translator's note: the source prints «متناد», a misprint for «متناه»] — several answers have been given to this question, among them:
1- What is narrated from al-Ḥasan; he said: «Allah the Exalted has not set a term for the people of the Fire; rather He said لابثين فيها أحقابا, and by Allah, it is only that whenever one ḥuqb passes another ḥuqb enters, forever; and the aḥqāb have no term except eternity.» 2- The word aḥqāb does not indicate an end; a single ḥuqb is finite, and the meaning is that they remain in it for aḥqāb in which they taste neither coolness nor drink except scalding water and pus; so the time limit is for the kinds of punishment, not a time limit for remaining and staying. (لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيها بَرْداً وَلا شَراباً) The clause لا يذوقون is a ḥāl of the pronoun in لابثين, i.e. remaining without tasting, so it is an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila); or an adjective of أحقابا; and it is said it is resumed. لا is negative; يذوقون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); فيها is attached to يذوقون; بردا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is a conjunction, لا is negative, and شرابا is conjoined to بردا. (إِلَّا حَمِيماً وَغَسَّاقاً) إلا is a particle of restriction, and حميما is a substitute of شرابا because the statement is non-affirmative, and غساقا is conjoined to it. This is easier than the path the exegetes took: some of them said it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), and al-Kashshāf followed this; he said: «They taste in it no coolness that relieves them of the heat of the Fire and no drink that calms their thirst, but they taste in it scalding water», and al-Jalāl followed him. Abū Ḥayyān said: «What appears is that it is connected, from His saying ولا شرابا.» (جَزاءً وِفاقاً) جزاء is a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, i.e. they were recompensed with that as a recompense; and وفاقا is an adjective of جزاء; so the clause is resumed. (إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا لا يَرْجُونَ حِساباً) The clause is a causal explanation of His saying جزاء. إنّ and its noun; the clause كانوا is the predicate of إنهم; كان and its noun, and the clause لا يرجون its predicate; حسابا is the object of يرجون, i.e. a reckoning. (وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا كِذَّاباً) The wāw is a conjunction; كذبوا is a verb and its agent; بآياتنا is attached to كذبوا; and كذابا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. a denying. The pattern fiʿʿāl for faʿʿala is all widespread in the speech of the eloquent Arabs; they hardly say anything else. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «One of them heard me explaining a verse and said: you have explained it with an explaining (fissāran) the like of which has not been heard. And it was read light, being the maṣdar of kadhaba, as evidenced by the saying:
فصدقتها وكذّبتها ... والمرء ينفعه كذابه»
(I told her the truth and I lied to her; and a man's lying benefits him.)
(وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْناهُ كِتاباً) The wāw is a conjunction; كل شيء is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), i.e. «and We counted everything; We counted it». This clause is parenthetical between the cause and its effect, for His coming saying فذوقوا is caused by their denial; and the benefit of the parenthesis is the confirmation of what He asserted in His saying جزاء وفاقا. The clause أحصيناه is explicative, with no grammatical position; أحصيناه is a past verb, its agent and its direct object. كتابا may be a maṣdar from the meaning of أحصيناه, i.e. a counting, with أحصيناه in the sense of «We wrote», because counting and writing meet in the meaning of recording and securing; or it is a maṣdar of أحصينا [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably «a maṣdar of an implied كتبنا» is meant]; and it may be a ḥāl in the sense of «written». (فَذُوقُوا فَلَنْ نَزِيدَكُمْ إِلَّا عَذاباً) The fāʾ is causal because it is — as we said — caused by their disbelief in the reckoning and their denial of the signs. ذوقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the meaning of the command is humiliation and contempt. The fāʾ is a conjunction; لن is a particle of negation, accusative and future; نزيدكم is an imperfect verb, accusative by لن, and the kāf is the first direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction, and عذابا is the second direct object. (إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفازاً) A resumed statement presented to set out the states of the people of Paradise. للمتقين is the fronted predicate of إنّ and مفازا the delayed noun of إنّ. al-mafāz is a mīm-maṣdar or a noun of place for the place of triumph. In al-Mukhtār: «al-fawz is salvation and attaining good, and it is also perishing; and the pattern of both is qāla.» On this basis, calling the waterless desert mafāza is literal, because it is a place of perishing, since among the meanings of al-fawz is perishing, as you have seen. In al-Qāmūs: «al-fawz: salvation, attaining good, and perishing — a contronym. fāza: he died; and fāza bihi: he attained it; and fāza minhu: he escaped it.» (حَدائِقَ وَأَعْناباً وَكَواعِبَ أَتْراباً وَكَأْساً دِهاقاً) حدائق is the plural of ḥadīqa, which is the round plot of land with palms and water; it is a part-for-whole substitute (badal baʿḍ min kull) of مفازا. أعنابا and what follows it are conjoined to حدائق, and there is no sense in conjoining them to مفازا on the argument that they were mentioned after the gardens to extol their status, for that is far from the ease of the Qurʾān and the absence of forced language in it. (لا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيها لَغْواً وَلا كِذَّاباً) The clause is a ḥāl of المتقين. لا is negative; يسمعون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the agent; فيها is attached to يسمعون; لغوا is the direct object and ولا كذابا is conjoined to لغوا. (جَزاءً مِنْ رَبِّكَ عَطاءً حِساباً) جزاء is an absolute object of an omitted verb, i.e. Allah recompensed them with that as a recompense; من ربك is an adjective of جزاء; and عطاء is a substitute of جزاء. In this substitution there is a subtle secret, namely the hint that this is a favour and a gift, while recompense is based on deserving. Al-Zamakhsharī parsed it as accusative by جزاء as its direct object, i.e. He recompensed them with a gift. حسابا is an adjective of عطاء, meaning «sufficient»; so it is a maṣdar put in place of the adjective, or it remains a maṣdar for intensiveness. (رَبِّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُمَا الرَّحْمنِ لا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطاباً) رب in the genitive as a substitute of ربك; and it was read in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. He is the Lord. ما is conjoined to السموات والأرض; بينهما is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما. الرحمن is also a substitute or adjective of رب. The clause لا يملكون is resumed; منه is attached to يملكون, and خطابا is the object. الرحمن was also read in the nominative, so it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause لا يملكون its predicate. (يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ صَفًّا لا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمنُ وَقالَ صَواباً) يوم is an adverb attached to لا يملكون or to لا يتكلمون; the clause يقوم الروح والملائكة is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; صفا is a ḥāl, i.e. standing in rows. The clause لا يتكلمون is an emphasis of His saying لا يملكون, or resumed. إلا is a particle of restriction; من is a substitute of the wāw in يتكلمون, or accusative by exception because the statement is non-affirmative. The clause أذن is the ṣila of من; له is attached to أذن, and الرحمن is the agent. قال is a past verb, its agent latent, implied as «he», and صوابا is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. a correct saying. (ذلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الْحَقُّ فَمَنْ شاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلى رَبِّهِ مَآباً) ذلك is the subject, اليوم a substitute and الحق the predicate of ذلك; you may also make اليوم the predicate and الحق an adjective of the predicate. فمن: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, because it discloses an omitted condition, as if it were said: and since the matter is of this standing, and as mentioned regarding the certainty of the said day, then whoever.... من is conditional, a subject; شاء is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the object of the willing is omitted; اتخذ is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis and its apodosis are the predicate of من. إلى ربه is attached to مآبا, and مآبا is the object of اتخذ. [Translator's note: in the source the following verse heading is fused into this line; it is separated here.] (إِنَّا أَنْذَرْناكُمْ عَذاباً قَرِيباً)
إنّ and its noun; the clause أنذرناكم is its predicate. أنذرناكم is
a verb, its agent and its first direct object; عذابا is the second direct object and قريبا an adjective. [Translator's note: here too the next verse heading is fused into the text in the source.] (يَوْمَ يَنْظُرُ الْمَرْءُ ما قَدَّمَتْ يَداهُ وَيَقُولُ الْكافِرُ يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُراباً)
يوم is an adverb attached to عذابا; the clause ينظر المرء is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; ما is the direct object, and the clause قدّمت يداه is the ṣila of ما. ويقول الكافر is conjoined to ينظر المرء; you may also make it resumed or circumstantial. يا is a particle of alerting, or the one addressed is omitted; ليتني: ليت and its noun; the clause كنت is its predicate, and ترابا is the predicate of كنت.

* Rhetoric:
Simile (tashbīh) is frequent in this sūra, and we point here to His saying «وسيّرت الجبال فكانت سرابا». It is an eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh) from which the particle has been omitted, and the point of resemblance has also been omitted, namely that what is seen is contrary to reality. Just as the mirage is seen from afar by the parched, burning-thirsty man as though it were water, so he rejoices at it and hurries to it, until when he reaches it after long weariness he finds it to be nothing — likewise the mountains are seen as if they were mountains, and they are not so in actual fact.
